chunks: And in the narration of Mūsā ibn Bakr, from al-Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

That a man from among the Muslims became Christian, so he was brought to ʿAlī عليه السلام. He asked him to repent, but he refused him. Then he seized his hair and said, "Trample him, O servants of Allah," so he was trampled until he died.

key_terms.فَاسْتَتَابَهُ: He asked him to repent and return.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the punishment for apostasy after refusing repentance?
ai.summary: This narration reports a case of apostasy in which a Muslim became Christian and was brought before Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام. After being asked to repent and refusing, he was executed. The report is relevant to discussions of legal rulings concerning apostasy in Shia fiqh.
